visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through
quiz.answers_at: Answers. One: five hundred plus two hundred

questions.q: Market cap 500, debt 200, cash 50. What's the enterprise value?
questions.explain: Equity value plus debt minus cash: 500 + 200 − 50 = 650. Adding the cash gives 750.
questions.explain_at: The simple version: equity value, plus debt, minus cash

questions.q: The company borrows 100 and keeps the cash. What happens to enterprise value?
questions.explain: Debt and cash both rise by 100 and cancel out. EV only changes when the business, or the market's view of it, changes.
questions.explain_at: Debt up a billion, cash up a billion. They cancel.

questions.q: Share price 20, 50 shares. What's the equity value?
questions.explain: Equity value is share price times the number of shares: 20 × 50 = 1,000.
questions.explain_at: For a listed company, it's simple: share price times the number of shares

questions.q: Which value goes with the P/E ratio?
questions.explain: Earnings come after interest, so they belong to shareholders: pair them with equity value.
questions.explain_at: Equity value belongs to shareholders only, so you pair it

questions.q: Equity value 100, no debt, cash 150. What's the enterprise value?
questions.explain: 100 + 0 − 150 = −50: the market values the business at less than the cash it holds.
questions.explain_at: Yes. If a company has more cash than its equity value plus its debt
